examples.en: The working title of this project is 'New Spring'.

examples.ko: 가칭이라서 이름이 나중에 바뀔 수도 있어요.
examples.en: It's only a tentative name, so it may change later.
I decided a tentative name for the new product and brought it to the meeting.
The new school's provisional name was announced as 'Future Middle School'.

examples.ko: 가칭 대신 진짜 이름을 빨리 정해야 해요.
examples.en: We need to choose the real name soon instead of a tentative one.
It was written as a tentative name in the presentation materials.

explain: 정식 이름이 정해지기 전에 임시로 부르는 이름이에요. 기사나 발표 자료에서 이름 뒤에 '(가칭)'이라고 붙여요. '가명'은 사람이 본명 대신 쓰는 이름이라 서로 달라요.

phrases.example: 아직 이름이 없어서 가칭으로 부르고 있어요.
phrases.en: It doesn't have a name yet, so we call it by a working title.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정식 이름이 없을 때 임시로 부른다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means calling it by a temporary name when there is no official one.
phrases.en_equiv: to call by a tentative name

phrases.en: I wrote 'Saebom (tentative name)' in the presentation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이름 뒤에 괄호로 붙여 임시 이름임을 알려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Added in parentheses after a name to show it is temporary.

phrases.en: At the meeting, we first decided on a working title.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정식 이름 전에 임시 이름을 정할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when choosing a temporary name before the official one.
phrases.en_equiv: to decide on a working title

explain_en: It is a temporary name used before the official one is set. In articles and slides you see (가칭) after a name. 가명 is different: it is a false name a person uses instead of their real one.

examples.ko: 기숙사에서는 규칙을 지키며 공동생활을 해야 해요.
examples.en: In a dormitory you have to follow the rules and live communally.

examples.ko: 공동생활에서는 서로 배려하는 게 가장 중요해요.
examples.en: In communal living, consideration for each other matters most.
Communal living was hard, so I started living on my own.
I lived communally for the first time at a retreat.

examples.ko: 친구 셋이 한 집에서 공동생활을 해요.
examples.en: Three friends live together in one house.
During shared living, we set up a cleaning duty roster.

explain: 기숙사, 합숙, 셰어하우스처럼 가족이 아닌 사람들이 함께 지낼 때 많이 써요. 함께 사는 가족에게는 보통 쓰지 않아요. '단체 생활'과 비슷하게 규칙과 배려가 떠오르는 말이에요.

phrases.en: I lived communally with friends in college.
phrases.nuance_ko: '하다'와 함께 써서 여러 사람이 같이 사는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '하다', it describes several people living together.

phrases.en: Please be sure to follow the communal living rules.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기숙사나 합숙에서 정한 약속을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It refers to rules set in dorms or group lodging.

phrases.example: 군대는 단체 생활이라서 혼자 있기가 어려워요.
phrases.en: The military is group living, so it's hard to be alone.
phrases.nuance_ko: '공동생활'과 비슷하지만 규칙을 따라야 하는 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '공동생활' but with a stronger sense of following rules.

explain_en: It is mostly used when people who aren't family live together, as in dorms, training camps or shared houses. It is usually not used for a family living together. Like '단체 생활', it brings rules and consideration to mind.

t90.ax: Three friends live together in one house.

examples.en: Liberation Day is August 15.
On Liberation Day, people hang the Korean flag in front of their homes.

examples.ko: 광복절이 금요일이면 사흘 쉴 수 있어요.
examples.en: If Liberation Day falls on a Friday, we get three days off.
On the morning of Liberation Day, I watched the ceremony on the news.

examples.ko: 광복절을 맞아 박물관에서 특별 전시를 열어요.
examples.en: The museum is holding a special exhibition for Liberation Day.
Last Liberation Day, I visited the Independence Hall with my family.

explain: 1945년 8월 15일에 일본에서 벗어난 것을 기념하는 국경일이에요. 한국에서는 쉬는 날이고, 이날 아침에는 대통령이 기념사를 해요.

phrases.en: Schools and companies are closed on Liberation Day.
phrases.nuance_ko: '에'를 붙여 광복절 '날'을 말할 때 써요. 날짜와 함께 일정을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '에' marks the day itself, used when talking about what happens on Liberation Day.

phrases.en: I watched the Liberation Day ceremony on TV.
phrases.nuance_ko: 광복절 아침에 열리는 공식 행사를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the official ceremony held on the morning of Liberation Day.

phrases.en: August 15 is Liberation Day, so we have the day off.
phrases.nuance_ko: 광복절을 날짜로 말하는 방법이에요. 이름 대신 날짜로 말하면 광복절이 무슨 날인지 설명하기 쉬워요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the date form of the holiday; saying the date helps explain which day Liberation Day is.

explain_en: It is the national holiday for August 15, 1945, when Korea was freed from Japanese rule, and it is a day off in Korea. The president gives a speech at the ceremony that morning.

examples.en: I pay the rent on the last day of every month.

examples.ko: 이번 달 말일까지 서류를 제출해야 해요.
examples.en: You have to submit the documents by the last day of this month.
At my company, payday is the last day of every month.
The last day of the month was a Sunday, so I deposited it a day early.

examples.ko: 말일 마감이라 이번 주는 정말 바빠요.
examples.en: The deadline is the end of the month, so this week is really busy.
I plan to move around the end of next month.

explain: 그 달의 마지막 날을 가리키고, 발음은 [마릴]이에요. '월말'은 달의 끝 무렵을 넓게 말하고, '말일'은 딱 마지막 하루를 말한다고 생각하면 돼요.

phrases.en: I'm busy at the end of the month because there's a lot of work.
phrases.nuance_ko: '말일'은 마지막 하루이고, '월말'은 달의 끝 무렵을 넓게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: 'Malil' is exactly the last day, while 'wolmal' means the end of the month more broadly.

phrases.en: You can apply until the end of this month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마감 날짜를 말할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for talking about deadlines.
phrases.en_equiv: until the last day of the month

phrases.en: I'm moving on the last day of this month.
phrases.nuance_ko: '말일'과 같은 뜻의 쉬운 표현이고 대화에서 편하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier way to say the same thing as 'malil', common in conversation.

explain_en: It points to the very last day of a month and is pronounced [마릴]. '월말' is looser, meaning roughly the end part of the month, while '말일' is that exact final day.

examples.en: Ants are lined up at the base of the tree.
The typhoon snapped the tree from its base.

examples.ko: 풀을 벨 때는 밑동 가까이를 잘라요.
examples.en: When cutting grass, you cut close to the base.
The base of a green onion is white and firm.

examples.ko: 베어 낸 나무의 밑동이 의자처럼 보여요.
examples.en: The stump of the felled tree looks like a chair.
The water rose up to the base of the pillar.

explain: 나무, 풀, 기둥처럼 길게 서 있는 것의 맨 아랫부분이에요. 뿌리 자체가 아니라 그 바로 위의 아랫부분을 가리켜요. 그냥 '아래'라는 뜻의 '밑'보다 구체적인 부분을 말해요.

phrases.en: I cut the tree all the way down to the base.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나무나 풀의 아랫부분을 베는 일에 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a phrase for cutting the bottom part of a tree or plant.

phrases.en: The base of the pillar had rotted, so we repaired it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나무뿐 아니라 길게 선 기둥의 아랫부분에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is used not only for trees but also for the bottom of any tall pillar.

phrases.en: This tree has a very thick base.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나무의 모양이나 크기를 설명할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this to describe the shape or size of a tree.

explain_en: It is the lowest part of something long and upright, such as a tree, plant or pillar. It refers to the lower part just above the roots, not the roots themselves. It is more specific than '밑', which just means 'underneath'.

t90.ax: Ants are lined up at the base of the tree.

examples.en: Student opinions are reflected in the class.
My idea was reflected in the plan.

examples.ko: 새 규칙은 다음 달부터 반영될 거예요.
examples.en: The new rule will take effect from next month.
So much was incorporated that the document got longer.
After the request was taken in, the menu changed.

examples.ko: 화가의 성격이 그림에 반영돼서 그림이 밝아요.
examples.en: The painter's personality shows in the painting, so it is bright.

explain: 의견, 요청, 성격 같은 것이 결과물 안에 들어가서 보일 때 써요. '~에 반영되다'처럼 '에'와 함께 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 사람이 의견을 넣으면 '반영하다', 결과에 들어가 있으면 '반영되다'예요.

phrases.en: My opinion wasn't reflected in the plan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 의견이 결과에 들어가지 않았다는 뜻의 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, meaning the opinion didn't make it into the result.

phrases.example: 화가의 성격이 그림에 잘 반영돼 있어요.
phrases.en: The painter's personality is well reflected in the painting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉으로 잘 보이게 들어가 있는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes something clearly showing in the result.

phrases.en: This is a new menu that reflects student opinions.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤 명사를 꾸며 줘요. 무엇이 들어간 결과인지 설명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It modifies the noun that follows and explains what went into it.

explain_en: Used when opinions, requests or personality get included in and show up in a result. It often takes '에': '~에 반영되다'. A person who includes it does '반영하다'; once it is in the result it is '반영되다'.

t90.ax: My idea was reflected in the plan.

examples.ko: 고속도로 옆에 방음벽이 높게 서 있어요.
examples.en: A tall soundproof wall stands beside the highway.

examples.ko: 방음벽을 세운 뒤로 소음이 많이 줄었어요.
examples.en: Since the soundproof wall was built, the noise has dropped a lot.
Thanks to the sound barrier, the house has become quiet.

examples.ko: 방음벽에 새 모양 스티커를 붙인 곳도 있어요.
examples.en: Some places put bird-shaped stickers on the sound barrier.

examples.ko: 방음벽 높이를 더 올려 달라고 주민들이 요청했어요.
examples.en: Residents asked for the sound barrier to be made taller.

examples.ko: 철도 옆 방음벽 때문에 창밖 풍경이 안 보여요.
examples.en: Because of the sound barrier next to the railway, I can't see the view outside the window.

explain: 주로 도로나 철도 옆에 세운 큰 벽을 말할 때 써요. 집 안의 소리 문제는 '방음이 잘 되다', '층간소음'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: They put up a soundproof wall in front of the apartment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소음을 막으려고 벽을 만드는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means building a wall to block noise.
phrases.en_equiv: to put up a soundproof wall

phrases.example: 도로 방음벽 때문에 바다가 안 보여요.
phrases.en: I can't see the sea because of the road sound barrier.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도로 옆에 있는 방음벽을 가리킬 때 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to refer to a sound barrier beside a road.

phrases.example: 방음벽이 높아서 차 소리가 잘 안 들려요.
phrases.en: The soundproof wall is tall, so I can hardly hear the cars.
phrases.nuance_ko: 벽의 높이와 소음 차단 효과를 함께 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about the wall's height together with its noise-blocking effect.

explain_en: It mostly refers to the large walls built beside roads and railways. For noise problems inside a home, people say things like '방음이 잘 되다' or '층간소음'.

examples.en: The upper floors of the building have offices.
In this apartment, the higher the floor, the better the view.

examples.ko: 비행기가 상층 기류 때문에 많이 흔들렸어요.
examples.en: The plane shook a lot because of upper-level air currents.

examples.ko: 불이 나자 상층 사람들이 먼저 대피했어요.
examples.en: When the fire broke out, the people on the upper floors evacuated first.

examples.ko: 그 파티에는 사회 상층 사람들만 모였어요.
examples.en: Only people from the upper class gathered at that party.

examples.ko: 바람이 센 날에는 상층 창문을 닫아 두세요.
examples.en: On windy days, keep the upper-floor windows closed.

explain: 아래쪽 '하층'과 짝이에요. 건물에서는 일상어로 '위층'을 많이 쓰고 '상층'은 설명 글에서 잘 써요. 사회에서 소득이나 지위를 나눌 때 '상층/중층/하층'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: The office is on the upper floor.
phrases.nuance_ko: '상층'과 비슷하지만 일상 대화에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 상층 but more common in daily talk.

phrases.en: You can see the whole city from the upper part of the building.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위쪽 부분을 조금 더 넓게 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the upper part more broadly.

phrases.en: That family lives on a high floor of the apartment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 높은 층에 사는 것을 설명하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes living on a high floor.
phrases.en_equiv: to live on the upper floors

explain_en: It pairs with '하층' (lower layer). For buildings, '위층' is the everyday word and '상층' fits explanatory writing. It is also used to divide society by income or status into '상층/중층/하층'.

examples.ko: 절 입구에 오래된 석상이 서 있어요.
examples.en: An old stone statue stands at the temple entrance.
Jeju Island has many stone statues like the dol hareubang.

examples.ko: 이 석상은 몇백 년 전에 만들어졌대요.
examples.en: They say this stone statue was made several hundred years ago.
Tourists take photos in front of the stone statue.

examples.ko: 비바람 때문에 석상의 얼굴이 많이 닳았어요.
examples.en: The statue's face is badly worn from wind and rain.
They set up a huge stone statue in the middle of the park.

explain: '석상'은 재료가 돌이라는 점이 핵심이에요. 같은 상이라도 청동으로 만들면 '동상'이라고 해요. 돌로 만든 불상은 '석불'이라고도 불러요.

phrases.en: They set up a stone statue at the entrance of the village.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상을 만들어 세운다는 뜻으로 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic pairing, meaning to erect a statue.

phrases.en: I took a photo in front of the stone statue.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사가 붙은 장소 표현으로 관광지 이야기에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: A place expression with a particle, common in talk about tourist spots.
phrases.en_equiv: in front of the stone statue

phrases.en: There are many old stone Buddha statues in Gyeongju.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돌로 만든 부처님 상만 가리키는 더 좁은 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A narrower word that refers only to a stone Buddha statue.

explain_en: The key point of '석상' is that it is made of stone. A statue made of bronze is called '동상' instead. A Buddha statue carved from stone is also called '석불'.

en: to be naive; to be unsophisticated

examples.ko: 그는 어수룩해 보여서 물건을 비싸게 샀어요.
examples.en: He looked naive and ended up buying the item at a high price.
He acts naive, but he's actually very smart.

examples.ko: 시골에서 올라온 청년이 어수룩해서 길을 헤맸어요.
examples.en: The young man who came up from the countryside was green and got lost.
He may sound unpolished, but he has a warm heart.
The green newcomer now works well.
He seems to grant every request because he is so naive.

explain: 순진하고 세상일에 서툴러서 조금 허술해 보인다는 느낌이에요. '순진하다'가 마음이 깨끗하다는 쪽이라면 '어수룩하다'는 남에게 쉽게 속을 것 같은 모습을 말할 때 더 어울려요.

phrases.en: You must not trick a naive person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세상일에 서툴러 쉽게 속을 것 같은 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a person who seems inexperienced and easy to fool.

phrases.en: That clerk looked naive.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이 순진하고 허술해 보일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone looks naive and a bit unguarded.

phrases.example: 그는 어수룩하지 않아서 쉽게 속지 않아요.
phrases.en: He isn't naive, so he doesn't get fooled easily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉과 달리 빈틈이 없다고 부정할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say someone is not naive and has no easy weak spots.

explain_en: It suggests someone who is simple and inexperienced in worldly matters, so they look a little careless. '순진하다' leans toward a pure heart, while '어수룩하다' fits someone who looks easy to fool.

en: to occur in succession; to be consecutive

examples.en: Rainy days keep coming one after another.
Even if failures continue in a row, I won't give up.
Good things kept happening in a row, so I feel great.
This is a stretch where accidents keep happening, so be careful.
If the overtime keeps going day after day, my body gets tired.
Don't use consecutive numbers as a password.

explain: 같은 일이나 상태가 끊기지 않고 줄줄이 이어질 때 써요. '일이 이어지다'보다 횟수가 여러 번이라는 느낌이 있어요. '연속 3일', '3연속'처럼 명사로도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: It rained for three days in a row.
phrases.nuance_ko: 며칠째 이어졌는지 말할 때 명사처럼 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used like a noun to say how many days in a row.

phrases.en: Hot days keep coming one after another.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금도 줄줄이 이어지는 중일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when things are still happening one after another.

phrases.en: I tried again despite the consecutive failures.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used to modify a noun that follows.

explain_en: Used when the same event or state follows one after another without a break. Compared with 이어지다, it stresses that it happens several times in a row. The noun forms are common too, like 연속 3일 and 3연속.

dis.h: happens one after another by itself
gh: do something repeatedly in a row

en: to be warm-hearted; to be sympathetic; to be kindhearted

examples.en: Grandmother is always warm toward her neighbors.

examples.ko: 인정스러운 주인 덕분에 밥을 공짜로 더 먹었어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the kind owner, I got extra food for free.
That man helped us warmheartedly.
I like the village because the people are warm.
I still remember my kind-hearted teacher.
His words are rough, but he has a kind heart.

explain: '인정'은 사람을 아끼는 따뜻한 마음이고, '인정스럽다'는 그런 마음이 겉으로 보인다는 뜻이에요. '정이 많다', '따뜻하다'보다 조금 옛날 느낌이에요. 같은 소리의 '인정하다(accept)'와는 전혀 달라요.

phrases.en: There are many warm-hearted people in our neighborhood.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ'을 붙여 사람을 꾸밀 때 쓰는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the form used to describe a person directly.

phrases.example: 가게 주인이 손님을 인정스럽게 대해 줘요.
phrases.en: The shop owner treats customers kindly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게'를 붙여 동사를 꾸미면 따뜻한 태도를 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-게' lets it describe how someone treats others.

phrases.example: 제 친구는 정이 많아서 모두가 좋아해요.
phrases.en: My friend is warm-hearted, so everyone likes her.
phrases.nuance_ko: '인정스럽다'보다 요즘 말이고 일상 대화에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more modern, everyday way to say the same thing.

explain_en: '인정' (human warmth) is a caring heart, and '인정스럽다' means it shows. It sounds a little more old-fashioned than '정이 많다' or '따뜻하다'. It is unrelated to '인정하다' (to accept).

examples.en: The bus is stopped at the bus stop.
The stopping time is usually one minute.

examples.ko: 이 도로에서는 정차를 할 수 없어요.
examples.en: You cannot stop on this road.
The train stops at Busan Station and then departs.
I paid a fine for illegal stopping.

examples.ko: 갑자기 정차하는 바람에 몸이 앞으로 쏠렸어요.
examples.en: The vehicle stopped suddenly, so my body lurched forward.

explain: '정차'는 차가 잠깐 서는 것, '주차'는 차를 세워 두고 자리를 비우는 것이라 달라요. 안내 방송과 표지판에 자주 나오고 '정차 금지', '정차 중'처럼 굳은 말로 알아 두세요. 일상에서 멈추는 건 '서다'를 써요.

phrases.en: The train is stopped at the station now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내 방송에서 자주 나오는 굳은 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A fixed phrase often heard in announcements.

phrases.en: This is a no-stopping zone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표지판에 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used on road signs.

phrases.en: The vehicle stopped suddenly and I was startled.
phrases.nuance_ko: 차가 갑자기 설 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a vehicle stops abruptly.

explain_en: '정차' is a vehicle stopping briefly; '주차' is leaving a parked vehicle, so they differ. It appears in announcements and road signs in fixed phrases like '정차 금지' and '정차 중'. In daily speech, 'to stop' is '서다'.

examples.en: The highway on-ramp was blocked, so I was late.

examples.ko: 우리 아파트 진입로는 좁아서 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: The access road to our apartment is narrow, so you need to be careful.
They closed the access road for a while because of construction.
Flowers are in full bloom along the park's entrance road.
A car slowly came in on the access road.
I heard they spread de-icer on the access road because of the snow.

explain: '진입로'는 큰길이나 고속도로, 건물로 들어가는 길이에요. '출구'는 나오는 곳, 진입로는 들어가는 곳으로 짝을 이뤄요. 교통 방송에서는 '진입로가 정체예요'처럼 자주 들려요.

phrases.en: The access road gets jammed in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 교통 방송에서 자주 듣는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing in traffic reports.

phrases.en: The road is narrow because of construction on the access road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길을 고치거나 넓히는 공사를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to work to repair or widen the road.

phrases.en: The car entered the highway.
phrases.nuance_ko: 진입로를 따라 들어가는 동작을 말하는 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb for entering by way of an access road.

explain_en: A 진입로 is the road you use to enter a main road, highway or building. It pairs with 출구, which is the way out. In traffic reports you often hear phrases like 진입로가 정체예요.
